result:
Review complete — verdict: **reject**.

The two Phase 4 script additions (exemption finalizer + `--suggest-fix`) are architecturally sound: additive, fail loudly on unmapped cases instead of guessing, and `--suggest-fix` never writes to source files. No injection/security issues found.

The blocker: the diff also commits `compliance-tracker-work` as a bare git gitlink (mode 160000) with no `.gitmodules` anywhere in the repo. I inspected the working tree and confirmed it's actually a full nested clone of the entire unrelated compliance-tracker project (AGENTS.md, drizzle/, bun.lock, etc.) — almost certainly scratch workspace content that got swept into the automated checkpoint commit. This would leave a dangling, unregistered commit reference in main history for anyone who clones the repo. Written to `review-verdict.json` with the finding and remediation (`git rm --cached compliance-tracker-work` + delete the nested clone before resubmitting).
